evidence: The hunk shows disconnect() only replaced pending.clear() with settlePendingOnClose while the close listener also clears the outbox; a message enqueued while connecting survives into the next connect(). 173b7ea adds the outbox splice, but places it before setState("closed"), which F7 then catches.
guidance_note: When rewriting one step of a teardown path that has a twin (disconnect vs close listener), diff the two paths step by step, including order, before pushing.

evidence: handleFrame's error branch only emitted an error and never settled the correlated pending entry, so the promise hung. The agent kept the diagnosis but used BRIDGE_INTERNAL instead of the reviewer's TMUX_ERROR, because tmux %error already resolves via ResponseFrame{success:false} and this frame comes from the bridge's outer catch. That is a defensible error-taxonomy correction, and the test in 173b7ea asserts it.
guidance_note: When a PR's goal is 'no pending promise hangs', enumerate every frame and event path that can terminate a request (close, disconnect, correlated error frame, post-close send) in the original change.

evidence: The original code was `.catch(() => {})` under a comment tagged [LAW:no-silent-failure]: an empty swallow labeled with the law it breaks. search-store already logged in its analogous catch, and 173b7ea adds console.warn to both.
guidance_note: Never write an empty catch under a no-silent-failure tag; if a rejection is fire-and-forget, log it at the moment you first add the catch.

evidence: The PR only added a .catch to insert(), so LLM-output sanitization in toSuggestion/parseSuggestions is out of scope, and the agent filed tmux-copilot-safety-nxj. The packet does not show toSuggestion or how sendKeys passes control characters, so whether an embedded \r actually executes cannot be confirmed here.
Six call sites had `.catch(() => {})`, unlike search-store's logging catch. 173b7ea replaces every one with a tagged console.warn, a full sweep of the class rather than one instance.
guidance_note: Pick one fire-and-forget rejection pattern (here: tagged console.warn) and apply it at every site in the original change, matching the precedent already in the codebase.

evidence: lastSentBytes was set optimistically and never rolled back once sendKeys could reject, so the right call was to accept. But 173b7ea resets to null unconditionally, with no ownership guard (F13). It also rolled back only this one optimistic value, leaving the same pattern in console-store, broadcast-store and store.ts (F8, F10-F12, F16, F17, F28, F29).
guidance_note: When rolling back optimistic state in an async catch, guard it with a per-call identity token from the start, and sweep every other store that writes optimistic state before the same now-rejectable call.

evidence: 173b7ea claims to mirror the close listener's teardown, but puts the outbox clear and settlePendingOnClose before setState("closed"), while the close listener runs setState first. At that point send() had no closed-state guard, so an onState("closed") reaction's execute() could land after the sweep and hang. The settle-before-setState order predates F1, but F1's fix repeated it for the outbox.
guidance_note: When a fix says 'mirror path X', copy X's ordering as well as its steps, and add a test that re-enters from the state-change fan-out.

evidence: The agent rejected this by citing the 'optimistic, self-correcting' design comment. In F28 it reversed itself, noting that clearTopology() is not called on a transient close, so a stale clientSessionId persists and wins in activeSessionId. The pushback deferred to an old comment without checking whether its premise still held once execute() could reject.
guidance_note: Before citing a documented design to reject a finding, re-check that the design's stated premise ('the event will correct us') still holds under the PR's new behavior.

evidence: The three concurrent execute() calls in jumpToPane are pre-existing, and 173b7ea only changed their catch bodies. The finding's claim that the failure was 'previously a visible unhandled-rejection' is wrong, because before this PR the WS bridge never rejected. Deferring to ticket tmux-optimistic-ui-7ue is a sound scope call. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: the logic is unchanged, and only the catch bodies were touched.

The subscribe catch left liveSig and disposeSubscription set after a rejection, so refresh() with the same signature no-oped forever; the agent admits the branch was newly reachable through this PR. The reviewer explicitly contrasts this with F6's rollback in escape-playground, the same gap F6's fix did not sweep. The fix in 415ef4a is guarded by liveSig.
guidance_note: Once a PR makes a previously never-rejecting call reject, list every caller that writes state before awaiting it and unwind each one in the same commit.

evidence: lastSend reports optimistic totals that are never corrected. The agent rightly notes that a blanket reset would misreport a partial success, and that a correct fix needs per-pane allSettled accounting, filed as tmux-optimistic-ui-7ue. But nothing in the code recorded the deferral, so the same finding came back as F12, F16 and F17.
guidance_note: When deferring a real finding, leave a one-line code comment at the site naming the ticket, so the next review round doesn't re-raise it.

evidence: This duplicates F11 in the same round. The reviewer offered 'or document why broadcast intentionally keeps optimistic counts', a cheap option the agent skipped; it replied on the thread but not in code, and the finding recurred twice.
guidance_note: Take the reviewer's 'or document it' option when deferring, so the deferral lives in the code where the next reviewer reads.

evidence: F6's fix in 173b7ea added an unconditional `lastSentBytes = null` in the catch, so an older send's late rejection wipes a newer send's value. Before the fix there was no reset at all, and the agent admits it saw this race and waved it off. The agent then applied the reviewer's value-equality guard verbatim (`lastSentBytes === sentBytes`), which collides on equal lengths and produced seven more findings (F18, F20, F22-F26).
guidance_note: Take a reviewer's diagnosis but write the cure yourself: an ownership check must compare identity (a monotonic token), never a value that two calls can share.

evidence: F7's fix (415ef4a) moved setState("closed") ahead of the sweep, so a handler that reconnects and issues a call during that fan-out now gets its new-connection entries swept by disconnect(). The close listener already had the same hazard. Deferring to tmux-ws-lifecycle-2vk was right, because the reviewer's options (document it, or a suppress flag) were weaker than the generation tagging that PR #155 then built. But the agent's claim that this is 'not a regression from this PR' is wrong for the disconnect path.
guidance_note: When reordering a teardown so that state handlers run before the sweep, decide in the same commit what a handler that reconnects should see, because ordering alone cannot tell old work from new.

evidence: 415ef4a unwound liveSig and disposeSubscription but left playgroundResult at {status:"idle"}, so the user sees idle forever, while runOneShot surfaces {status:"error"} in the same field. ee17192 sets the error variant.
guidance_note: When unwinding a failed operation, reset every field it set, including what the user sees, not just the internal bookkeeping, and match the sibling path's error surface.

evidence: This re-raises F11: broadcast-store.ts was unchanged in 415ef4a and the inconsistency with escape-playground's rollback still stands. The agent consistently pointed to the filed ticket. The round was spent only because the deferral left no trace in the code.
This is a third re-raise of the broadcast lastSend finding, in the same round as F16. The agent's reply points to tmux-optimistic-ui-7ue; the reply-hint 'unclear' is just a 'same finding as' opener.

ee17192's guard `if (this.lastSentBytes === sentBytes)` compares values, so send("ab") then send("cd") both write 2, and A's late rejection clobbers B. 6c7cfab switches to a monotonic sendToken, and its ABA test asserts the fix.
guidance_note: Test ownership guards with two calls that produce identical observable values; a test that uses different values can't tell identity apart from equality.

evidence: requestSuggestions() is untouched by the PR, and the reviewer itself calls the race 'benign in practice (last-write-wins)'. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: ee17192 never touched copilot-store.ts.
Same ABA collision as F18 (identical text sent twice), introduced by the value guard in ee17192 and fixed with sendToken in 6c7cfab.

The totalLines and empty-line counting are pre-existing; the PR only wrapped the backfill in try/catch, and the reviewer itself says 'pre-existing' and 'design-adjacent'. This is a naming nit, not a defect. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive because ee17192 never touched search-store.ts.
Duplicate of F18, raised by a different scope in the same round. The byte-value guard from ee17192 is fixed by the token in 6c7cfab.
Duplicate of F18: with the value comparison, `2 === 2`, a stale rejection from an earlier same-length send nulls a successful newer one. Fixed in 6c7cfab.
Same ABA collision, plus the observation that the ee17192 test only uses 2 vs 5 bytes. Fixed with sendToken and a same-length test in 6c7cfab.
Fifth copy of the byte-value ABA finding in round 3, all caused by the value guard the agent took verbatim from F13. Resolved by 6c7cfab's token.
The ee17192 regression test used 'ab' (2 bytes) against 'hello' (5 bytes), so it could not catch a value-equality guard. 6c7cfab adds the 'ab' vs 'cd' test.
guidance_note: Write the regression test so it would fail against the weakest plausible fix: for a 'stale writer' race, use two writers whose values are equal.

evidence: send() registered pending entries and enqueued with no closed-state check, so a call after disconnect() hung forever. This gap was in the original send() and is named as pre-existing in the round 0 and round 1 summaries, not created by 6c7cfab, so the flag is a false positive. It is fixed in 4e91ccf.
guidance_note: When the PR's invariant is 'no promise hangs', treat 'call issued after teardown' as one of the cases to cover in the first commit, and act on the reviewer's pre-existing-gap notes in the summary, not only on the inline threads.

evidence: This re-raises F8, contrasting with EscapePlaygroundStore's rollback. The agent reversed its round-1 pushback after finding that clearTopology() does not run on a transient close, so the stale id persists. It fixed this in 4e91ccf with a token-guarded revert and store.test.ts. This round's work existed only because F8 was wrongly rejected.
jumpToPane sets clientSessionId optimistically in the same way and never reverts it, the same gap as F28. Fixed in 4e91ccf with the shared sessionSelectToken and a jumpToPane test.

narrative: The PR made WS-bridge promises actually reject, which turned every optimistic-state write before a fire-and-forget call into a latent bug. F6's fix rolled back one such value (escape-playground) with an unguarded reset. That spawned F13, and the agent then applied the reviewer's value-equality guard verbatim, which spawned seven ABA duplicates in round 3. The same gap went unswept in console-store, broadcast-store and store.ts. Broadcast was correctly deferred but re-raised three times, and the store.ts pushback (F8) was wrong and reversed in round 4 (F28/F29). Separately, F1's 'mirror the close listener' fix got the ordering wrong (F7). That reorder imported the reconnect-sweep hazard (F14), which became PR #155, and its comment about entries landing in pending became stale once F27 added send()'s closed-state guard (flagged as #155/F2).
guidance_observations: When the PR changes a call from never-rejecting to rejecting, grep every caller and classify each one's pre-call state writes in the first commit instead of letting the reviewer find them one store per round.
Reviewer-proposed cures were taken verbatim twice (F13's value guard); the diagnosis was right and the cure was the local-minimum one.
Deferrals lived only in thread replies, so the reviewer re-raised the same broadcast finding in three rounds; a code comment naming the ticket would have closed it.
Pre-existing gaps named in round summaries (send() post-close hang) were left until a later round raised them inline, costing a round.

evidence: connect()'s guard excludes only OPEN/CONNECTING. With the old socket CLOSING, the generation bump and the reassignment of this.ws make the old close listener no-op (`this.ws !== ws`), and disconnect() now sweeps only the current gen, so old-gen entries hang. The agent chose the reviewer's second option (sweep before bump) and explained why gating on CLOSING would not clean up the orphan. The fix introduced F4.
guidance_note: When replacing a sweep-everything teardown with a per-generation one, enumerate every way a generation can lose its owner (CLOSING reconnect, constructor throw) before pushing.

evidence: send()'s `state === "closed"` guard (added in #154 by F27's fix) rejects before a pending entry is ever created, so the comment claiming such entries 'land in pending' is false. The drift dates from #154 (F7's comment, contradicted by F27's fix), and this PR rephrased the comment without correcting it. e87c9d4 rewrites it accurately.
guidance_note: When editing a comment that explains why an order matters, re-verify the claim against the current code, not just the wording.

evidence: Every call site already wrapped sweepGeneration in runInAction, so nothing was broken and this is a convention point. Declaring it as an action matches setState/enqueue/drainOutbox. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: the missing annotation predates e87c9d4, whose new call site was wrapped. But ff7976b also silently dropped `private` from sweepGeneration, which caused F7.
guidance_note: When a fix requires changing a member's visibility, say so in the reply and look for the mechanism the codebase already uses to annotate private members, rather than widening access quietly.

evidence: e87c9d4 added a pre-reconnect sweepGeneration that can emitError synchronously before this.ws is reassigned, and the agent itself says 'previously nothing inside connect() called emitError synchronously'. A reentrant connect() from an error handler orphans a socket. ff7976b adds a connecting flag cleared in finally, plus a socket-count test.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a call that runs caller-supplied handlers inside a method that is mid-way through a state transition, check for reentrancy in the same commit.

evidence: emitError ran caller handlers via forEach before the outbox filter and the pending reject loop, so a throwing handler aborted cleanup. b60581b moves notification last and adds a throwing-handler test. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: the emit-before-cleanup order is in the original sweepGeneration hunk, not introduced by ff7976b.
guidance_note: In teardown code, finish all of the object's own state changes before invoking any caller-supplied callback.

evidence: Promise reject() only enqueues .catch reactions as microtasks and never runs them inline, so a throwing consumer handler cannot interrupt the for loop; the pushback is correct on spec grounds. The cited law is about null guards, and the agent admits it applies 'outside its literal null-check scope'. The flag is a false positive, since the reject loop predates ff7976b.

ff7976b (F3's fix) dropped `private` from sweepGeneration. The agent claims there is 'no generic-argument workaround' and that it only tried `makeObservable<WebSocketBridge>`. But the AnnotationsMap<T, AdditionalFields> it quotes has a second parameter for exactly this, and the sibling EscapePlaygroundStore in #154 already uses `makeAutoObservable<this, "bridge" | ... | "sendToken">` to annotate private members. The pushback rests on a false claim, and the method stayed public.
guidance_note: Before declaring a type-system constraint insurmountable, grep the repo for the same API's existing usage; here the private-member pattern was already in a sibling store.

evidence: The generation bump and setState("connecting") ran before `new WebSocket(url)`. If the constructor throws, entries a 'connecting' handler created carry a generation that this.ws never represents. If this.ws is null on the next connect, the guarded pre-sweep skips them. The order is in the original connect(), so the flag on b60581b is a false positive. aec3952 moves both lines after construction.
guidance_note: Commit to a new generation only after the resource that owns it has been constructed successfully.

narrative: PR #155 implemented the generation tagging deferred from #154/F14. Replacing the sweep-everything teardown with per-generation sweeps opened an orphaning hole on a CLOSING reconnect (F1). Its fix added a synchronous emitError inside connect(), which opened a reentrancy window (F4). Accepting a convention-level 'declare as action' finding (F3) silently made sweepGeneration public. When the reviewer flagged that (F7), the agent pushed back with an incorrect claim that MobX cannot annotate private members, although a sibling store does exactly that. Each round also carried a pre-existing finding (F5, F8), so no round would have been skipped with perfect fixes.
guidance_observations: Switching from a global sweep to a scoped one changes who owns orphaned work; enumerating the owner-loss paths up front would have pre-empted F1 and F8.
A fix's reply described the action annotation but not the visibility change it forced; undisclosed side effects in a fix commit are what the next round catches.
A 'can't be done' pushback was not checked against existing code in the same repo.
